newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BT makes TNT bid difficult for KPN.
newsitem.headline: BT makes TNT bid difficult for KPN.

text.p: An express freight firm such as Federal Express Corp may take advantage of the raid on TNT Ltd's share register by Bankers Trust and launch a counter-bid to Koninklijke PTT Nederland (KPN), analysts said.
But potential rivals would be hard-pressed to make a more generous offer than KPN's A$2.45 per share cash bid for the struggling international transport firm, they said.
"I think they (BT) are just waiting to see if someone else comes and makes a higher offer. I think there is a small chance that FedEx could come and offer slightly higher," one said.

BT said after the close of trade on Tuesday that it had spent about A$43 million on the purchase of 18.04 million TNT shares, or three percent, since the bid was announced last Wednesday, paying between A$2.38 and A$2.43 per share.
BT now has a blocking stake of 19.99 percent and told Reuters the offer price was at the low end of its range of valuations. It would not say if it would accept the KPN bid.
"Personally, I don't think there is more room for that (the offer price) to move upwards. I think the current offer is fairly generous," said analyst Paul Xavier at BNP Equities.
